title: The source file is v2 in its name and Version 1 in its own table, with the date 28 October 2026
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx
description: The file of the family is named v2, and the table at the top of the document says Version 1 and Date 28 October 2026. The family has no change log and no earlier version in the folder, so the two numbers cannot both be the version of the surviving document. The next version has to be named, and the version it continues has to be stated without breaking either number of the source.
evidence: The source file name 'Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx'; its own table rows 'Version | 1' and 'Date | 28 October 2026'; the folder 05 Technical architecture holds no v1 file and no other version of the family; Rules v1 §R8.2 (the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1).
owner_role: Technical documentation with the architecture team
proposed: The file name carries the family version, so the next version is v3 and the change log starts at 3; the source is recorded as 2 as the file name and 1 as the version in its own table, and both numbers are kept in the metadata row 'Source version'.

title: No recovery point objective and no recovery time objective is set for any store or any service
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 2 gives the recovery point objective and the recovery time objective the value 'The ACE value' with the status 'Open, DL11', and never says what the ACE value is. Architecture v5 slide 48 records 'RPO/RTO: not yet set' and an NFR gap with 'proposed tiers', and no tier appears in any source of this run, neither per store nor per service. With 19 schemas in one instance the value is per store and not per service, and the source has no wording for the Temporal persistence database or for the Kafka topics that the target architecture adds.
evidence: v2 section 1 rows 'Recovery point objective' and 'Recovery time objective' ('The ACE value', 'Open, DL11'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48 ('Service targets (NFR v3) ... RPO/RTO: not yet set' and 'NFR gap: RPO/RTO are not set in NFR Spec v3; proposed tiers'); v2 section 3 row on the zone-redundant PostgreSQL server; Temporal and Drools design L1 (Temporal persistence in its own database) and slide 27 (30 days retention, archived to Blob).
owner_role: RWB-PLT-DB with SCB IT infrastructure, confirmed by Compliance and Operations
proposed: Every per-store row carries the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B-TECH-11-2; ASM-B-TECH-11-2)' and no tier or number of minutes is invented. The gap is closed by RWB-PLT-DB with SCB IT infrastructure before the first production release, and the restore test records the measured time until the target exists.

title: The source sends report queries to the data lake copy, and the target architecture removes the data lake
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 2 scaling bullet 2 says that read queries for reports go to the data lake copy and not to the live database. Architecture v5 removes the data lake and gives rwb-reporting (P9) a read model built from the events, and DP-17 retires the lake paths. The source has no statement of where a report query goes once the lake is gone, and the bullet cannot be kept as written without contradicting the target architecture.
evidence: v2 section 3 bullet 2 ('read queries for reports go to the data lake copy, not the live database'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (no data lake) and slide 41 (P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard, regulatory reports); Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17 ('Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 - Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting'); JOB-15 owner P9 (regulatory extract, no data lake).
proposed: The bullet is rewritten to the rwb-reporting read model built from the events (ADR-018), and the sentence keeps its two prohibitions: not the 19 live schemas, and not a data lake.

title: The load figures of the source and Architecture v5 differ, and the source has no 2031 row
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: The load table of version 2 gives about 23,600 open cases at go-live, about 26,500 at the end of 2027, about 410 online in the busiest hour and about 21 requests a second. Architecture v5 slide 33 and its notes give about 23,570, about 26,479, 414 concurrent internal users and the same 21 requests a second, and add about 47,389 open cases by 2031. The source stops at 2027 and has no 2031 row, so the capacity horizon of the design is shorter than the architecture's.
evidence: v2 section 2 rows 'Open cases at go-live', 'Open cases at the end of 2027', 'Online in the busiest hour', 'Requests a second in the busiest hour'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 33 and slide 48 notes ('23,570 today, 26,479 by end 2027, 47,389 by 2031 ... 414 concurrent internal users is ~21 requests a second at peak'); Volume and Scale Forecast v3 and NFR Spec v3 as cited there.
owner_role: Architecture with the performance test owner
proposed: The seven rows of version 2 are kept word for word, the difference is stated as under 0.2 percent and read as the same forecast, and the 2031 figure is added in the new section 2.1 with its source.

title: The source is written for one recovery module and has no per-service target, size or deployment shape
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 2 says the ACE service scales out and that 'the recovery module adds no separate service', and it gives one set of service levels for the module. Architecture v5 has 19 services with 19 schemas, 19 topics, 19 task queues and 19 deployments, and sets its targets per service ('Service targets (NFR v3)'). The source has no target per service, no deployment shape, no rule for whether the targets are the same for all 19, and no statement of what a screen sees when it composes two services.
evidence: v2 section 3 bullet 1 and its section 1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 33 ('all 19 services have the same shape ... API deployment 2 pods for availability ... worker deployment scaled by KEDA') and slide 48 ('Service targets (NFR v3): 99.9% in business hours ... RPO/RTO: not yet set'); Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.1.
proposed: A per-service availability table (19 rows) applies the same two targets, the shape of one service is written once and repeated, and the composed screen is stated as the product of the services it calls, inside the one-hop call budget.

title: No per-topic sizing exists for the 19 topics; one topic is sized in the architecture
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.docx
description: Architecture v5 slide 22 sizes one topic, rwb.payment.events.v1, at 12 partitions, replication factor 3 and 7 days retention, and names the retry topics and the dead-letter topic. The 19 remaining topics, including rwb.decision-record.v1, have no sizing row in any source, and the source document has no per-topic row at all. The design therefore cannot state a partition count per service from a source.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 22 ('rwb.payment.events.v1 key caseId - 12 partitions - RF 3 - 7 days'; retry 1 min / 10 min / 1 h then .dlt + alert) and slide 11 (retry topics and dead-letter topic with alert); v2 section 3 and section 5 have no topic row; Rules v1 §R4 (topic rwb.<short>.events.v1 with retry and .dlt topics).
proposed: The call-type table states the retry and dead-letter policy as the target for every topic, the per-topic partition count is written as the one sized topic read as the default until RWB-PLT-EVT sets it per service, and the open point is recorded in the change table.

title: The edge components have no owner row in the Ownership Map, and section 5 needs one
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx
description: Version 2 has a row 'Partner gateway down' and a screen response target that are met at the edge, and the Ownership Map has no row for gateway-bff and no row for the partner gateway: the 19 service rows, the 93 table rows, the 156 operation rows and the 22 job rows name neither component. The design must name an owner for both without inventing a service code.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheets Services, Tables, Endpoints, Workflows and activities and Jobs; v2 section 1 row 'Screen response' and section 5 row 'Partner gateway down'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (gateway-bff composes the screen) and slide 35 (partners only through the partner gateway); Rules v1 §R4 (edge: gateway-bff with the Redis session store, and the partner gateway in the DMZ) and §R5.1 (RWB-PLT-EDGE).
proposed: The screen response level is owned by RWB-PLT-EDGE for the composition, and the partner gateway row is read as RWB-PLT-EDGE with S9 rwb-partner behind it; the component row is added to the map at the next revision.

title: The source sets no monitoring or alerting target, and a per-service failure needs one
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx
description: Version 2 lists degraded modes and tests but names no monitoring target, no alerting threshold and no detection time, because with one module the on-call was the module's. With 19 services, the failure of one service has to be detected per service, and ADR-023 makes observability a per-service concern. The source has no availability measurement rule, no error budget, no alert threshold and no statement of who is alerted.
evidence: v2 sections 1, 5 and 6 (no monitoring row and no alert row); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 34 (failure of one service is contained) and slide 35 (one trace across services); Rules v1 §R5.1 (RWB-PLT-OBS); ids.json and Rules v1 §R8.4 (ADR-023 observability per service).
proposed: Version 3 names RWB-PLT-OBS as the owner of the per-service detection and alerting and records that no threshold exists; the threshold belongs to ADR-023 and to the observability platform story, not to this document.

title: The 07:00 deadline of the COLLINS load is one number for a chain of services, with no per-service deadline
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 2 gives 'COLLINS load complete - By 07:00' as one service level for the module. Architecture v5 slide 33 describes the 05:00 to 07:00 chain as case creation, payment matching, allocation and rebalance in three services (rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation) with the ACE data read in rwb-source-data, so the deadline is shared by four owners and the source does not say how it is divided or which service is measured.
evidence: v2 section 1 row 'COLLINS load complete' ('By 07:00', 'Proposed'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 33 ('05:00-07:00 morning run: rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation') and slide 48 ('the 05:00-07:00 chain: case creation, payment matching, allocation, rebalance'); Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet (JOB-04 owner P1, JOB-07 owner P8, JOB-02, JOB-03 and JOB-06 owner P3).
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data with P3 rwb-case and P8 rwb-payment
proposed: The level stays as written and is owned by P1 with P3 and P8 named in the same chain, and the per-step deadline is left to the batch and scheduling design rather than invented here.

title: The failover test and the restore test of the source have no story in the split plan
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json
description: Version 2 names four tests and one story, RWB-TE-009, which the split plan carries as RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG. The failover test of the database and the restore test of documents and the database are named without a story, and the split plan has no story whose title is a failover or a restore test, so the tests have no build owner in the plan that the realignment uses.
evidence: v2 section 6 bullets 1 to 4; split_plan.json legacy RWB-TE-009 slice RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG and legacy NF-06 slice RWB-PLT-NF06-DB; no legacy key in the split plan covers a failover or a restore drill.
owner_role: QA team suggested, with RWB-PLT-DB and P5 rwb-document
proposed: The load test stays with RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG, the failover test is owned by the database story RWB-PLT-NF06-DB with the ACE DBA, and the restore test by P5 rwb-document with RWB-PLT-DB; the detection of a missing story is recorded rather than a story being invented.
